anchors.paper_title: Movement‐induced hypoalgesia: behavioral characteristics and neural mechanisms
anchors.paper_venue: Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences
anchors.reason: Paper studies movement-induced hypoalgesia with five experiments (129 participants) from Li Hu's lab; the dataset is laser pain rating, and no concrete match to this specific dataset is evident.

metadata.methods_description: Laser stimulation intensity was calibrated per participant to the energy corresponding to a mean rating of 7. Participants then received 10 laser stimuli while fixating on a crosshair with eyes open. After each stimulus there was a 5-second pause, followed by ratings of pain intensity and unpleasantness on a 0-10 NRS, given by mouse click on a screen axis (decimal values allowed). The next trial began randomly 5 seconds after the rating.
